tour.overview:
The Douro Valley is best enjoyed slowly. Spending a night at a quinta, among the terraced vineyards, lets you see the valley at sunset and sunrise, taste more wines and meet the families who make them. Nearby, the town of Lamego is known for its baroque sanctuary of Nossa Senhora dos Remédios, reached by a stairway of nearly 700 steps.

This private two-day tour shows the valley with a licensed guide, a vehicle and a night at a wine estate.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 2 days, 1 night
• Start and end: your hotel in Porto
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver; 1 night at a quinta with breakfast and dinner
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability, your quinta and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• Three quintas.
• A cooking class.
• A boat trip.
• Lamego.
• The Douro railway.

WHY THIS WORKS
The night at the quinta transforms the experience: quiet evenings among the vines and an unhurried pace.

WHO IT SUITS
Couples, wine lovers and food lovers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For a single day, choose our Douro Valley day tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The harvest is in September and early October. Some quintas close in winter; we choose those open.

days.name: Into the Douro: Lamego, a cooking class and a night at a quinta
days.description:
What to expect: the valley, a cooking class and an evening at a wine estate.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 9:00 and drive into the valley. In Lamego, you climb or drive up to the sanctuary of Nossa Senhora dos Remédios, with its zig-zag baroque stairway decorated with azulejos and fountains.

At a quinta, you join a cooking class with the family, preparing dishes such as cod, roast kid or a Douro stew with vegetables from the garden, followed by lunch with their wines. In the afternoon, you check in to your quinta, walk among the vines and taste its ports, and watch the sun set over the terraces before dinner with wine.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Pick-up in Porto.
10:45 – Lamego sanctuary.
12:00 – Cooking class and lunch.
15:30 – Check-in at your quinta and tasting.
Sunset – Walk among the vines.
20:00 – Dinner.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Many quintas have a pool for summer afternoons.

INCLUDED: vehicle, guide, cooking class, lunch, tasting, dinner.
NOT INCLUDED: extra drinks.

Overnight: wine quinta in the Douro.
Meals: lunch, dinner.

days.name: A boat trip, the Douro railway, another quinta and back to Porto
days.description:
What to expect: the river by boat and by train.

After breakfast, you take a boat trip on the river from Pinhão, then board the historic Douro railway, which runs along the riverbank between vineyards and through tunnels, to Régua or Tua, where your driver meets you. A final tasting at a third quinta, perhaps focused on old tawnies, completes the visit before you drive back to Porto.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Breakfast.
10:30 – Boat trip from Pinhão.
12:00 – Douro railway.
13:30 – Lunch break.
15:00 – Third quinta and tasting.
18:00 – Back in Porto.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A historic steam train runs on summer weekends; it can be booked.

INCLUDED: vehicle, guide, boat, train, tasting.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: breakfast.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability, hotels and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: What kind of quinta is used?
faq.answer: A family wine estate with comfortable rooms, often with a pool and river views.

faq.question: Are meals included?
faq.answer: Lunch and dinner on day 1 and breakfast on day 2.

faq.question: Can non-drinkers join?
faq.answer: Of course; the food and the landscape are a highlight.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Children are welcome; tastings are for adults.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
Can we take part in the harvest?
faq.answer: Yes, in September, with grape picking and treading at some quintas.

faq.question: Can we add a third day?
faq.answer: Yes, to explore the upper Douro or the Côa rock art.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes, layers and swimwear in summer.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to October. September is the harvest.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not obligatory in Portugal, but rounding up or leaving 5 to 10 percent for a guide or driver you were happy with is appreciated.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
